source_book: Sri Chaitanya — FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students, Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring. Stems restated in our own wording; the mathematics is exact. No solution content from the source book appears in this file, by policy.
section_banners: Very Short Answer Questions : (Q1-27, printed pp. 9-15)
Theorems: (1-6, printed pp. 17-19) — the book's own banner; it is NOT one of VSAQ/SAQ/LAQ, so `section` records it verbatim as THEOREMS rather than being re-labelled.

questions.stem: If A = {0, π/6, π/4, π/3, π/2} and f: A→B is a surjection defined by f(x) = cos x, find B.
If A = {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2} and f: A→B is a surjection defined by f(x) = x² + x + 1, find B.
If A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and f: A→R is a function defined by f(x) = (x² − x + 1)/(x + 1), find the range of f.
If f: R − {0} → R is defined by f(x) = x³ − 1/x³, show that f(x) + f(1/x) = 0.
If f: R → R is defined by f(x) = (1 − x²)/(1 + x²), show that f(tan θ) = cos 2θ.
questions.notes: The book's own MODEL PAPER-IA puts this exact question at Q3, Section I (VSAQ).

questions.stem: If f: R − {0} → R is defined by f(x) = x + 1/x, prove that (f(x))² = f(x²) + f(1).

questions.notes: Q7 prints one set f and four separate operations i)-iv); each is independently answerable, so one object per part.

questions.stem: If f: R→R and g: R→R are defined by f(x) = 3x − 2 and g(x) = x² + 1, find (gof⁻¹)(2).
If f: R→R and g: R→R are defined by f(x) = 3x − 2 and g(x) = x² + 1, find (gof)(x − 1).
If f(x) = (x + 1)/(x − 1), x ≠ ±1, find (fofof)(x).
If f(x) = (x + 1)/(x − 1), x ≠ ±1, find (fofofof)(x).
If f(x) = 2, g(x) = x² and h(x) = 2x for all x ∈ R, find (fo(goh))(x).
questions.notes: The single star sits on the number 10 and so covers both parts. Q10's two parts have DIFFERENT setups, so they are two objects. The printed bracketing of this part reads (fo(goh)(x)) — one closing bracket short.

questions.stem: Find the domain of the real valued function f(x) = √([x] − x), where [x] is the greatest integer not exceeding x.

If f(x) = (sin²x + cos⁴x)/(cos²x + sin⁴x), show that f(2016) = 1.
If f is defined by f(x) = 3x − 2 for x ≥ 3, f(x) = x² − 2 for −2 ≤ x ≤ 2 and f(x) = 2x + 1 for x < −3, find the values of f(4), f(2.5), f(−2), f(−4), f(0) and f(−7).
questions.notes: The three printed branches leave (−3, −2) and (2, 3) undefined. That gap is deliberate — 2.5 is asked precisely because it falls in it — so it is not a misprint.

questions.stem: If f is defined by f(x) = x + 2 for x > 1, f(x) = 2 for −1 ≤ x ≤ 1 and f(x) = x − 1 for −3 < x < −1, find the values of f(3), f(0), f(−1.5), f(2) + f(−2) and f(−5).
questions.notes: The single star on 23 sits on the (a) block; (b) carries none of its own. Again the branches leave gaps, and −5 is asked because it falls outside them.

questions.notes: The book's own MODEL PAPER-IA puts this question at Q11, Section II (SAQ) — the paper's single Functions short-answer slot.

questions.stem: Show that f: Q→Q defined by f(x) = 5x + 4 is a bijection, and find f⁻¹.
questions.notes: Two demands in one stem: prove the bijection, then invert. The right edge of printed p.16 clips the tail of the stem; the value 5x + 4 is fixed by the worked block below it.
Q4 prints TEN operations i)-x) over one pair of sets; each is independently answerable, so one object per part.

questions.stem: Let f: A→B and g: B→C be bijections. Show that gof: A→C is a bijection.
questions.notes: The book's banner for this block is Theorems: — it is neither VSAQ nor SAQ, and the book prints no LAQ banner anywhere in this chapter.

questions.stem: Let f: A→B and g: B→C be bijections. Show that (gof)⁻¹ = f⁻¹og⁻¹.
Let f: A→B and let I_A and I_B be the identity functions on A and B. Show that foI_A = f = I_Bof.
Let f: A→B be a bijection. Show that fof⁻¹ = I_B and f⁻¹of = I_A.
questions.notes: FOUR stars — the only 4-star prefix in the chapter, and the highest rank the book uses anywhere in it. The gutter is intact here, so the count is a reading.

questions.stem: Let f: A→B be a function. Show that f is a bijection if and only if there is a function g: B→A with fog = I_B and gof = I_A, and that g = f⁻¹ in that case.
Let f: A→B, g: B→C and h: C→D. Show that ho(gof) = (hog)of, that is, that composition of functions is associative.
